findings.claim: total() does not validate that array elements are finite numbers; NaN or Infinity entries will silently corrupt the sum.
findings.evidence: No type-runtime check or filter before reduce; TypeScript types alone do not prevent NaN at runtime.

findings.claim: discounted() does not clamp or validate the percent parameter; values >100 produce negative results, and negative percents produce amounts greater than the original.
findings.evidence: Math.round(cents  (1 - percent / 100)) — with percent=200, result is cents  -1; with percent=-50, result is cents  1.5.

findings.claim: discounted() does not guard against non-integer cent values as input, risking floating-point drift before Math.round.
findings.evidence: If cents is already a fractional value (e.g., 99.5), multiplying by a fraction and then rounding may produce off-by-one results compared to expectations.

findings.claim: No test coverage for edge cases: empty array passed to total, zero discount, discount exceeding 100%, or negative values.
findings.evidence: Only two happy-path assertions exist: total([125,75]) and discounted(1000,10). No boundary or invalid-input scenarios are tested.

findings.claim: No test coverage for non-integer or floating-point inputs.
findings.evidence: Both assertions use clean integers (125, 75, 1000, 10). Floating-point rounding behavior of total and discounted is never exercised.

findings.claim: File is a bare script with no test framework; failures produce unhelpful output and non-standard exit behavior.
findings.evidence: Tests are plain if/throw statements rather than using a test runner (e.g., vitest, node:test). A failure yields only a generic Error with no diff or context.

findings.claim: Import uses .js extension which may fail depending on TypeScript module resolution settings.
findings.evidence: import { discounted, total } from "../src/pricing.js" — if tsconfig does not enable NodeNext/Node16 module resolution or the project is not configured for ESM with .js extensions mapping to .ts, this import can fail at compile time.
